areas.body:
## Big houses make a different kind of laundry list

A plotted house in DLF Phase 1 has floor-to-ceiling drapes in two or three rooms, rugs that nobody wants to roll up and carry anywhere, sofa covers that have quietly gone two shades darker, and a linen cupboard that gets restocked rather than rotated. That is the work we are most often asked for here, and it is the work that is hardest to do at home. Heavy lined curtains do not fit a domestic machine, and a rug that is washed without being dried properly comes back smelling worse than it went.

So the visit itself is different. Curtains have to come down before we can take them, and rehanging is the part people forget to plan for, so we agree a day rather than a two-hour window and we tell you honestly how long the panels will be away. Rugs and sofa covers are counted piece by piece at your door like everything else, with a written receipt, because these are the items where a missing panel is noticed weeks later.

## The wardrobe half of the job

Alongside the household textiles there is a steady, unglamorous formal load: cotton shirts and trousers pressed properly, sarees and suits that go out for dry cleaning rather than a wash, and woollens that come out for six weeks of Delhi NCR winter and then want cleaning before they go back into storage. Leather jackets and bags get treated as the separate craft they are, not thrown in with the rest.

Our Vyapar Kendra counter in Sushant Lok Phase I, Sector 43 is the closer of our two shops to Phase 1, so this is a short run for us. Pickup and delivery are free. Call or WhatsApp **+91 63 67 600 500** and tell us what is coming down off the rails.

Curtain and upholstery jobs are booked as a day rather than a slot, because panels have to be taken down before we can carry them and rehung after they come back.
Carpets, rugs and sofa covers are counted piece by piece at pickup and covered by a written receipt.
Nearest walk-in counter: Wash4You Vyapar Kendra, Gate No. 3, Shop No. 180, GF Shushant, Vyapar Kendra Road, Block C, Sushant Lok Phase I, Sector 43, Gurugram 122009.

faqs.a: Yes, and end-of-winter is exactly the right time to send them. Woollens are dry cleaned before storage so moth damage has nothing to feed on; leather is handled as its own specialist process, never alongside a normal dry-clean load.

### A rental catchment with an office wardrobe

Phase 2 sits close enough to the office towers that people rent here specifically to avoid the commute, and the housing reflects it: builder floors, shared flats, a lot of one- and two-year tenancies. The basket is predictable in a way that actually helps us. Four or five shirts a week that want a proper wash and press rather than dry cleaning, trousers that need a crease and not a solvent, and the small number of expensive things — a suit, a blazer, a winter coat — that genuinely do need dry cleaning and usually arrive once a season rather than once a week.

The details that matter on a shirt are collars, cuffs and the antiperspirant residue that yellows a white shirt from the inside long before the fabric wears out. We treat those specifically rather than hoping a hot wash covers it.

### Timing and shared flats

Two practical things shape pickup here. First, nobody in this catchment is home at two in the afternoon, so we work early-morning, post-seven and weekend windows and do not pretend otherwise. Second, shared flats are the norm, and three people's clothes should never come back as one bundle. Every order is counted with the person who booked it, at their door, packed separately from every other customer's order, and covered by a written receipt.

Sneakers are the other standing request — a pair worn to the metro every day picks up more than the owner expects, and mesh, canvas, leather and suede each get handled differently. Free pickup and delivery. Call or WhatsApp **+91 63 67 600 500**.

## The weekly load, done properly

The households here are mostly settled ones, and settled households produce steady laundry rather than dramatic laundry. School uniforms that have to be back and pressed for Monday. Office cottons. Bedsheets and towels in quantity. It is the least glamorous category we handle and the one where consistency matters most, because you notice immediately if a shirt comes back with a limp collar or a sheet comes back short.

So we count everything with you at the door, both directions, and pack your order separately from every other customer's. That sounds like a small thing until the week a single school shirt goes missing.

## Then the four times a year that are different

Around the weekly rhythm sit the exceptions. Festive and wedding wear — sarees, lehengas, sherwanis, anything with zari or beadwork — which goes through dry cleaning and hand attention rather than a wash cycle, because the threadwork is the first thing a normal process damages. Winter quilts, blankets and woollens, which come out in November and want cleaning again in March before they are stored. And the occasional disaster: turmeric, oil, a child and a pen.

On stains, we would rather be honest than optimistic. Tell us what caused it and what you have already tried at home, because a mark that has been scrubbed with the wrong thing behaves differently, and knowing that changes what we attempt first.

Pickup and delivery are free across Gurugram. Call or WhatsApp **+91 63 67 600 500**.

faqs.q: When should I send quilts and blankets?
faqs.a: Twice a year works best — once before they come out in winter, and again at the end of the season before they go into storage. Storing a quilt dirty is what turns a small stain into a permanent one.

faqs.q: I already tried to wash a turmeric stain out. Is it worth sending?
faqs.a: Usually yes, but tell us what you used on it. Home attempts change how the stain sits in the fibre, and we would rather know than guess.

## When the cost of getting it wrong is the whole point

The garments we are asked for here are not difficult because they are dirty. They are difficult because they are expensive and because the wrong process is irreversible. Silk loses its fall. Wool felts. A structured blazer that is pressed flat never gets its shape back. Leather that is cleaned like fabric dries out and cracks.

So these do not go through one generic process. Dry cleaning is the right answer for suits, blazers, wool trousers, silk and most embellished wear. Leather and suede — jackets, bags, shoes — are a separate craft handled separately. Bags with hardware and lining are their own job again. If we are not sure a piece will respond, we will say so before we take it rather than after.

## Collection from a tower, without the guard desk

High-rise living adds a step: a gate desk, a visitor entry, sometimes a call up before we are allowed in. That is fine, and we work with whatever your building requires. What we do not do is hand your order over at the security desk and call it collected. The count is done with you at your flat door, your order is packed separately from every other customer's, and you get a written receipt at pickup. For a one-off designer piece rather than a weekly bundle, that receipt is the whole point.

Alongside the wardrobe there is the soft-furnishing work these flats generate — lined drapes, sofa covers, rugs — which we collect on an agreed day rather than a two-hour slot.

Pickup and delivery are free. Call or WhatsApp **+91 63 67 600 500**.

Home linen — curtains from one room at a time rather than the whole house, the odd rug — and, in a catchment with a lot of tenancies, the deep clean that happens when someone moves in or moves out and wants the mattress, sofa and curtains dealt with before the furniture is arranged.

A managed township means a visitor desk and an entry log, and that is genuinely easier than a street of independent gates once it is set up. faqs.a: A heavier, closed-in smell and a damp feel after a humid stretch are the usual signs. It is cleaned at your flat as a booked appointment, so tell us the size and how many beds when you call.

faqs.q: Can I hand over clothes, linen and a quilt in one go?
faqs.a: Yes, and most orders here are exactly that mix. They are separated during the count at your door and each type is handled by the right process, but you only deal with one pickup and one receipt.

faqs.q: There is nowhere nearby to walk in. Do I have to come to your shop?
faqs.a: Not at all. The doorstep service is designed for exactly this situation and the full count and receipt happen at your door. The Arcadia counter in Sector 49 is there if you ever want it, but almost nobody from this sector uses it.

faqs.q: Why does a quilt take longer than clothes?
faqs.a: The drying does. Filling holds water long after the outer fabric feels dry, and a quilt returned damp will smell within a week. We would rather keep it a day longer and tell you that at pickup.
